Olhe para a reta de cima: 5/10 é a metade do caminho entre 0 e 1. Na reta de baixo, qual é a marca que também fica exatamente na metade do caminho?

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta exibida "Five tenths equals how many fourths?"; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 1, uma acima da outra: na Linha 1 a fração dada já está marcada pelo tutor; na Linha 2 o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividir (campo de denominador + confirmar) e marca o ponto da fração equivalente; à direita das retas, a igualdade entre as duas frações é mostrada em caixas: as da esquerda vêm preenchidas e, na da direita, o aluno digita o NUMERADOR (o denominador alvo já aparece); há também um seletor de comparação ("≟", "=", "≠") entre as duas frações; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir a Linha 2, marcar o ponto, digitar o numerador, comparar, concluir).

dicas.texto: What does the word fourths tell you about the number of equal parts?
Use the denominator field for Line 2, then confirm the number of equal intervals.
The target fraction must have a denominator that matches the requested unit, fourths.
Enter the number of equal parts named by fourths and confirm the division of Line 2.
Equivalent fractions name the same location between 0 and 1.
Compare the marked position on Line 1 with the equal intervals on Line 2.
The marked location is halfway from 0 to 1, so look for the quarter mark at the same halfway position.
Select the Line 2 segment whose endpoint is aligned with the marked point on Line 1, then submit that fraction.
A point represents a value by its position on the interval from 0 to 1.
Find the point on Line 2 that is horizontally aligned with the mark on Line 1.
The target point is at the midpoint of the line, not at the first or last quarter mark.
Click the quarter mark located halfway between 0 and 1, then submit the fraction emitted by the line.
The numerator counts how many equal parts are included from 0 to the marked point.
Keep the denominator as 4 and count the Line 2 intervals reached by the marked point.
The point lies at the halfway location, after counting the equal fourths from the left endpoint.
Count the intervals from 0 through the marked point and enter that count in R1_user.
Equivalent fractions represent the same amount, even when their denominators differ.
Compare the positions of the two marked fractions on the interval from 0 to 1.
The two marks are aligned at the same location, so the fractions do not show different amounts.
Select the sign that means both sides represent exactly the same quantity: =.
Before finishing, check that the fraction, point, numerator, and comparison sign all agree.
Review the marked point on Line 2 and the numerator shown in the fraction comparison.
Make sure the comparison sign states equality and that the right fraction uses fourths.
After confirming every field, press the button that submits the completed work.
